newsitem.title: VATICAN: Italian farmers light Christmas bonfire at Vatican.
newsitem.headline: Italian farmers light Christmas bonfire at Vatican.

text.p: Thousands of Italian farmers and artisans took part in an ancient Christmas rite on Sunday when they lit a bonfire in St Peter's Square to celebrate the birth of Christ, "the light of the world".

Citizens from the central region of Molise carried 2,000 wooden torches into the square and piled them into a blazing bonfire in the "Ndocciata" rite, observed at Christmas in their town of Agnone for hundreds of years.
Pope John Paul briefly addressed the crowd from the window of his Vatican apartment, thanking them for coming and wishing them a happy holiday.

Earlier, the Pope laid a wreath of flowers at the base of a statue of the Virgin Mary, who Roman Catholics believe was without original sin, at Rome's Spanish Steps in a traditional ceremony marking the feast of the Immaculate Conception.
